title: Daskam 38 — The Birth of Sri Krishna
description: Sri Krishna appears to Devaki and Vasudeva, assumes the form of an infant, and begins the journey to Gokulam.

stanzas.sanskrit:
आनन्दरूप भगवन्नयि तेऽवतारे
प्राप्ते प्रदीप्तभवदङ्गनिरीयमाणैः ।
कान्तिव्रजैरिव घनाघनमण्डलैर्द्या-
मावृण्वती विरुरुचे किल वर्षवेला ॥ ३८-१ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: As the Lord's incarnation approached, the rainy sky appeared suffused with the radiance of his cloud-blue form.
stanzas.commentary_en: When the time of the incarnation came, the sky was covered with rain-bearing clouds. It shone like the radiant blue complexion of the Lord, whose brilliance spread everywhere.
stanzas.translation_en: Thou O Lord! Who are Bliss personified, when the time of Thy incarnation approached, the rainy season indeed shone with the lustre of Thy body, which emanated the blue rays of brilliance on the thick dark clouds that covered the skies.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ānandarūpa bhagavannayi te’vatāre
prāpte pradīptabhavadaṅganirīyamāṇaiḥ |
kāntivrajairiva ghanāghanamaṇḍalairdyā-
māvṛṇvatī viruruce kila varṣavelā || 38-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
आशासु शीतलतरासु पयोदतोयै-
राशासिताप्तिविवशेषु च सज्जनेषु ।
नैशाकरोदयविधौ निशि मध्यमायां
क्लेशापहस्त्रिजगतां त्वमिहाऽविरासीः ॥ ३८-२ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: At midnight, as rain cooled every direction and the moon rose, Krishna appeared to remove the sorrows of the three worlds.
stanzas.commentary_en: Rain cooled the earth, the moon emerged and shone at midnight, and virtuous people rejoiced as their hopes neared fulfilment. At that auspicious moment, the Lord who removes the sorrows of all three worlds incarnated on earth as Sri Krishna.
stanzas.translation_en: When all the directions had been well cooled by the rain waters, when the virtuous people were overwhelmed with the joy of the impending fulfillment of their desires, and the moon was rising at midnight, Thou the remover of all sorrows, appeared here on this earth, embodied as Krishna.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
āśāsu śītalatarāsu payodatoyai-
rāśāsitāptivivaśeṣu ca sajjaneṣu |
naiśākarodayavidhau niśi madhyamāyāṃ
kleśāpahastrijagatāṃ tvamihā’virāsīḥ || 38-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
बाल्यस्पृशापि वपुषा दधुषा विभूती-
रुद्यत्किरीटकटकाङ्गदहारभासा ।
शङ्खारि वारिज गदा परिभासितेन
मेघासितेन परिलेसिथ सूतिगेहे ॥ ३८-३ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Though newly born, Krishna revealed his divine form, crowned and adorned, bearing the conch, discus, lotus, and mace.
stanzas.commentary_en: At birth, Sri Krishna appeared in a fully revealed divine form. His cloud-blue body shone with a sparkling crown, bracelets, armlets and necklaces, and he bore the conch, discus, lotus and mace.
stanzas.translation_en: Thou shone in the birth chamber, though in the from of a child, with Thy body adorned with the divine majesties, shining crown, bracelets, shoulder ornaments, beautiful necklace, conch, discus, lotus, mace, beautiful as the hue of the rain bearing clouds.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bālyaspṛśāpi vapuṣā dadhuṣā vibhūtī-
rudyatkirīṭakaṭakāṅgadahārabhāsā |
śaṅkhāri vārija gadā paribhāsitena
meghāsitena parilesitha sūtigehe || 38-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
वक्षःस्थलीसुखनिलीनविलासिलक्ष्मी-
मन्दाक्षलक्षितकटाक्षविमोक्षभेदैः ।
तन्मन्दिरस्य खलकंस कृतामलक्ष्मी-
मुन्मार्जयन्निव विरेजिथ वासुदेव ॥ ३८-४ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: The radiance of Lakshmi dwelling upon Krishna's chest dispelled the prison's inauspicious darkness created by Kamsa.
stanzas.commentary_en: Mahalakshmi dwelt resplendently upon the Lord's cloud-blue chest. Her gracious sidelong glances brightened the prison chamber and seemed to sweep away the evil and inauspiciousness created by Kamsa.
stanzas.translation_en: O Vaasudeva! Thou did shine in that prison house with the glorious Lakshmi Devi comfortably resting on Thy bosom. The side glances of varied graces, with shyful eyes, cast by her, dispersed away the inauspiciousness of the prison caused by the wicked Kansa.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
vakṣaḥsthalīsukhanilīnavilāsilakṣmī-
mandākṣalakṣitakaṭākṣavimokṣabhedaiḥ |
tanmandirasya khalakaṃsa kṛtāmalakṣmī-
munmārjayanniva virejitha vāsudeva || 38-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
शौरिस्तु धीरमुनिमण्डलचेतसोऽपि
दूरस्थितं वपुरुदीक्ष्य निजेक्षणाभ्याम् ।
आनन्दबाष्पपुलकोद्गमगद्गदार्द्र-
स्तुष्टाव दृष्टिमकरन्दरसं भवन्तम् ॥ ३८-५ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Seeing the form difficult even for sages to behold, Vasudeva was overcome with tears, horripilation, and devotion.
stanzas.commentary_en: On beholding the Lord directly, Vasudeva's eyes filled with tears of joy and his whole body thrilled with goosebumps. His throat choked with overwhelming devotion, and in a melting voice he began to praise the Lord.
stanzas.translation_en: Thy form which is unapproachable to the minds of many aspiring sages, when Vasudeva saw with his own eyes, he had horripilation all over his body, his eyes were full of tears of joy and with a choked and melting voice he sang Thy prises, whose sight is like nectar honey for the bee like eyes.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śauristu dhīramunimaṇḍalacetaso’pi
dūrasthitaṃ vapurudīkṣya nijekṣaṇābhyām |
ānandabāṣpapulakodgamagadgadārdra-
stuṣṭāva dṛṣṭimakarandarasaṃ bhavantam || 38-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
देव प्रसीद परपूरुष तापवल्ली-
निर्लूनदात्र समनेत्र कलाविलासिन् ।
खेदानपाकुरु कृपागुरुभिः कटाक्षै-
रित्यादि तेन मुदितेन चिरं नुतोऽभूः ॥ ३८-६ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Vasudeva prayed that the Lord's compassionate glance would cut away the creeper of suffering and remove all sorrow.
stanzas.commentary_en: Vasudeva praised the Lord for a long time. He prayed that the Lord would remove every sorrow and suffering through his playful, sword-like eyes and compassionate sidelong glances.
stanzas.translation_en: Thou were praised with prayers for a long time by Vasudeva who was filled with joy, saying that 'O Lord! cut down the creeper of all my sorrows with Thy sharp sword like playful eyes. O Supreme Being! Remove all my sufferings with Thy side glances laden with compassion.'
stanzas.stanza_roman:
deva prasīda parapūruṣa tāpavallī-
nirlūnadātra samanetra kalāvilāsin |
khedānapākuru kṛpāgurubhiḥ kaṭākṣai-
rityādi tena muditena ciraṃ nuto’bhūḥ || 38-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
मात्रा च नेत्रसलिलास्तृतगात्रवल्या
स्तोत्रैरभिष्टुतगुणः करुणालयस्त्वम् ।
प्राचीनजन्मयुगलं प्रतिबोध्य ताभ्यां
मातुर्गिरा दधिथ मानुषबालवेषम् ॥ ३८-७ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: After reminding Devaki and Vasudeva of their two former births, the merciful Lord answered his mother's prayer and became an ordinary infant.
stanzas.commentary_en: Devaki's slender body was bathed in tears of joy as she prayed to the Lord. The merciful Lord reminded his parents of their two previous births and, at his mother's request, exchanged his revealed divine form for that of a human infant.
stanzas.translation_en: And by Thy mother Devaki's tears whose delicate creeper like body was covered and made wet, Thy excellences were praised by hymns. Thou, the abode of mercy, then explained to them, Thy parents, about their two previous births. Then at the request of Thy mother Devaki, Thou assumed the form of a human infant child.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
mātrā ca netrasalilāstṛtagātravalyā
stotrairabhiṣṭutaguṇaḥ karuṇālayastvam |
prācīnajanmayugalaṃ pratibodhya tābhyāṃ
māturgirā dadhitha mānuṣabālaveṣam || 38-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वत्प्रेरितस्तदनु नन्दतनूजया ते
व्यत्यासमारचयितुं स हि शूरसूनुः ।
त्वां हस्तयोरधित चित्तविधार्यमार्यै-
रम्भोरुहस्थकलहंसकिशोररम्यम् ॥ ३८-८ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Prompted by the Lord, Vasudeva lifted the infant to exchange him with Nanda's daughter; the child resembled a young swan resting on lotus-like hands.
stanzas.commentary_en: The Lord instructed Vasudeva, son of Shurasena, to carry the infant and exchange him with Yogamaya, the daughter born to Nandagopa. Resting in Vasudeva's hands, the divine child looked like a graceful young swan perched upon a lotus.
stanzas.translation_en: At Thy prompting, in order to bring about Thy inter-exchanging with the daughter of Nanda, the son of Shoorasena Vasudeva took Thee in his two hands. Thou who can only be conceived in the minds of the sages, in Vasudeva's hands looked like an attractive young swan perched on a lotus.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvatpreritastadanu nandatanūjayā te
vyatyāsamāracayituṃ sa hi śūrasūnuḥ |
tvāṃ hastayoradhita cittavidhāryamāryai-
rambhoruhasthakalahaṃsakiśoraramyam || 38-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
जाता तदा पशुपसद्मनि योगनिद्रा
निद्राविमुद्रितमथाकृत पौरलोकम् ।
त्वत्प्रेरणात् किमिव चित्रमचेतनैर्य-
द्द्वारैः स्वयं व्यघटि सङ्घटितैः सुगाढम् ॥ ३८-९ ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Yogamaya sent the people into deep sleep, and at Krishna's prompting the firmly locked prison doors opened by themselves.
stanzas.commentary_en: Yogamaya, born in Nandagopa's house, caused the people to fall into deep sleep. At the Lord's prompting, even the heavily secured prison doors opened by themselves so that Vasudeva could carry the infant away.
stanzas.translation_en: Thereafter, at Thy behest, Yoga-Maayaa, who was born in the house of Nandagopa, caused all the people in the region to fall into deep slumber. This is not at all surprising, considering that the well locked inanimate doors of the prison opened by themselves.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
jātā tadā paśupasadmani yoganidrā
nidrāvimudritamathākṛta pauralokam |
tvatpreraṇāt kimiva citramacetanairya-
ddvāraiḥ svayaṃ vyaghaṭi saṅghaṭitaiḥ sugāḍham || 38-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
शेषेण भूरिफणवारितवारिणाऽथ
स्वैरं प्रदर्शितपथो मणिदीपितेन ।
त्वां धारयन् स खलु धन्यतमः प्रतस्थे
सोऽयं त्वमीश मम नाशय रोगवेगान् ॥ ३८-१० ॥
stanzas.meaning_en: Vasudeva set out carrying Krishna while Adishesha sheltered them from the rain and lit their path; Bhattathiri closes by praying for relief from illness.
stanzas.commentary_en: Blessed to carry the Lord as his child, Vasudeva set out for Gokulam. Adishesha spread his many hoods over the infant to shield him from the rain, while the jewels upon those hoods illuminated the path. Bhattathiri asks Guruvayurappan, the Lord of such glory, to cure his ailments.
stanzas.translation_en: He, Vasudeva, the most blessed one set out carrying Thee in his hands. Aadi Shesha with his many hoods warded off the rain waters and led along the way by him with the gems on his hoods enlightening the way. O Lord! Of such exceeding prowess deign to save me from my forceful ailments.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śeṣeṇa bhūriphaṇavāritavāriṇā’tha
svairaṃ pradarśitapatho maṇidīpitena |
tvāṃ dhārayan sa khalu dhanyatamaḥ pratasthe
so’yaṃ tvamīśa mama nāśaya rogavegān || 38-10 ||
